issues.body: The prior-round defect remains in `executes_needle`: `text.startswith(needle)` has no shell-word boundary, while `needle in text` has no exact contiguous argv-word boundary. Thus `scripts/tests/test_sweeper.py.disabled --verbose` can satisfy the direct-execution pin for `scripts/tests/test_sweeper.py`, and `python3 scripts/sweeper.py --self-test-disabled` can satisfy the interpreter pin for `sweeper.py --self-test`, even though neither exact pinned invocation executes. The added self-test cases still do not cover either mutation.
issues.fix_hint: Tokenize the masked command representation and compare complete words: require the needle token sequence to equal the leading argv sequence for direct execution, or an exact contiguous argv subsequence for recognized interpreters. Add failing `check_tree` fixtures for a suffixed executable path and a suffixed `--self-test` option, plus controls showing legitimate trailing arguments remain accepted.
issues.title: S1 still accepts command-name and option superstrings

verdict.summary: Round 6 is stagnant: the round-5 major finding remains unchanged. `executes_needle` still accepts character-prefix and unrestricted substring matches rather than exact shell-word sequences, and the self-test still omits the two requested superstring mutations. Consequently S1 can stay green after the exact pinned executable or option stops running.
